query: What can Cedar Lantern customers do with the billing export today, what are its current limits, and what is planned next?

source_chunks.heading: Customer operations note — 12 March 2026
source_chunks.content:
Cedar Lantern sells a warehouse scheduling service to distributors. Its billing export is a customer-controlled report rather than an accounting integration. Account administrators open Settings, select a month, and download a CSV showing completed appointments and the associated charge for each location. The export includes the local appointment date, warehouse identifier, and charge amount. The report is generated when the administrator requests it, so two downloads may differ if a completed appointment was later corrected by the operations team. The CSV is intended to help finance teams reconcile a monthly invoice; it is not a tax document and does not itself pay or modify an invoice. Customers have asked for richer grouping, but the current interface has only the month selector and the location identifier in each row. Administrators can download prior closed months as well as the current month. The current month may be incomplete until the month ends. For internal troubleshooting, support asks the administrator for the export month and account name rather than a copy of the entire file. The support team can compare the selected period with invoice line items and explain timing differences without making changes to the customer account.
 
- The current export is a manually downloaded CSV for one selected month.
- Only account administrators can generate it.
- A month may contain corrections made after a prior download.

source_chunks.heading: Billing export boundaries — support handbook, 13 March 2026
source_chunks.content:
The downloadable file is available to accounts on all paid plans. The permission check follows the current account administrator role, not the role of the person who originally created the account. Removing an administrator immediately removes their access to future downloads. Customer support can explain what each column means, but support staff cannot generate a customer export from the support console. For privacy, customer success should avoid asking users to email a full file; a redacted example of an unexpected row is usually enough to investigate a discrepancy. Amounts are expressed in the currency used on the invoice for the account. The file has no conversion column, and any comparison between accounts in different currencies needs to happen outside the product. This matters for a distributor with several independently billed accounts, because each account generates its own report and has its own invoice. A user can reconcile those reports externally, but cannot select multiple accounts in the current export screen.

The export does not run on a schedule or send files by email. It has no API and cannot export more than one account at a time. These are product limits as of this note, not temporary incidents or permission errors. The team has no commitment to provide a combined multi-account report.

source_chunks.heading: Product planning record — 18 March 2026
source_chunks.content:
The billing team reviewed requests from six account administrators who reconcile appointments against monthly invoices. Several wanted to receive an export without signing in on the first working day of each month. Others wanted the same rows to flow into their existing bookkeeping system. The team grouped these requests separately because delivery by email requires permissions and retention decisions, while a programmatic interface requires an authentication design and public documentation. The team agreed that a missing feature should not be described as a customer-specific configuration issue. Support may share the current manual workflow and record the customer's desired delivery format, but should not promise an implementation date. No customer request in this review altered the current one-account scope, and no decision was made to introduce cross-account consolidation. The roadmap is a statement of intent and remains subject to engineering review, security review, and competing priorities. It is not evidence that a customer can use the feature today.

The team plans to pilot scheduled email delivery with a small group in the third quarter of 2026. An export API is only under consideration; it is not approved or scheduled.
